jokes.label: Joke A
jokes.title: Remote Work
jokes.joke: I signed up for my company’s mind-transfer program because they promised I’d never have to commute again. They uploaded my consciousness into the office network. Now I can answer email, attend meetings, and update spreadsheets without a body. I asked my boss what happens when I retire. He said, “We delete your account.” Apparently I didn’t achieve immortality—I became software with a pension.

jokes.label: Joke B
jokes.title: Backup Body
jokes.joke: I did a mind transfer last year, moved my consciousness into a younger body. Best decision I ever made. New body, new confidence, walked into work like I owned the place. Turns out I did own the place, I forgot to transfer my bank account too, so now some twenty-two-year-old intern is confidently spending my retirement while I'm stuck explaining to HR why I keep answering to two names.

jokes.label: Joke C
jokes.title: Family Boundaries
jokes.joke: My mom has an incredible amount of confidence in her ability to run my life from three states away. She called me yesterday during a job interview, and when I declined the call, she immediately texted: "Don’t accept their first offer, sit up straight, and order the soup."

jokes.label: Joke D
jokes.title: Lateral Soul Move
jokes.joke: I was so done being an office worker I signed up for experimental mind transfer. Figured I'd wake up as a pilot or at least a guy who doesn't live for the weekend. Nope. They put me in the body of the guy in the next cubicle. Same fluorescent lights, same passive-aggressive emails, just a slightly different view of the water cooler. Turns out my soul only qualified for a lateral transfer.

jokes.label: Joke E
jokes.title: Factory Reset
jokes.joke: I tried this new productivity hack where you ‘swap minds’ with a super-efficient coworker. Turns out his brain runs like a factory—loud, stressed, and everything smells faintly of burnt plastic. I lasted ten minutes before begging to switch back. Now I’m just an office worker with the confidence of a man who survived OSHA violations inside his own head.

scores.comment: The mind-transfer premise has potential, but the bank-account/intern logic is unclear and the HR ending dilutes rather than sharpens the payoff.
Clean, relatable setup with efficient escalation; 'order the soup' is an unexpected, concrete final turn that lands well.
Strong first-person construction and a clear final pun; 'lateral transfer' neatly resolves both seed concepts, though the destination twist is somewhat foreseeable.
The OSHA-inside-my-head image is amusing, but the joke clearly uses Factory and Confident in addition to Mind Transfer and Office Worker, violating the exactly-two-seeds requirement.
Clean escalation to a pension-software punchline; solid but the twist is fairly telegraphed.
Relatable mom-meddling bit with a specific, funny capper ('order the soup') that lands well.
Good subversion of the expected upgrade fantasy; 'lateral transfer' pun ties it together nicely.
Funny OSHA line, but leans on factory and confidence as extra concepts beyond the two claimed.
Logical premise with clean flow, but the punchline lands on an expected corporate trope rather than a strong laugh.
Convoluted turn that gets tangled in logistics; the double identity payoff loses comic momentum.
Strong stage rhythm and a crisp final turn with 'lateral transfer' that delivers a genuine snap.
Stuffs extra seed concepts (factory, confident) beyond two, and the closing line peters out without a hard hit.
Clean mind-upload corporate bit; pension closer works but lands mild.
Strong body-swap premise with effective bank-account and dual-name turn.
Familiar distant-mom interference; light and competent but forgettable.
Uses more than two seed concepts; factory image and OSHA closer feel forced.
Clean premise with a tidy software-immortality turn that lands a mild, coherent laugh.
Fun escalation and a clear first-person rhythm, though the final beat is more amusing than sharp.
A relatable interference angle with a neat punch, but the joke stays small and lightly humorous.
Strong timing and a memorable lateral-transfer turn make this a genuinely good joke.
